narrative.overview: FinTrack reads like a well-kept ledger: quiet slate surfaces, dense but legible numbers, and three accents that always mean the same thing. It borrows the focus of a dark-first night desk and the friendliness of a pocket planner.
keyCharacteristics: Slate neutrals in light and dark, switched by a .dark class on CSS variables.
Emerald, amber and rose are semantic money colors, never decoration.
Bold small uppercase labels over medium-weight body text.
Generous rounded corners (12-16px) on every interactive surface.

rules.name: The Money Meaning Rule
rules.body: Emerald means in or good, rose means out or destructive, amber means attention.

rules.name: The Dual Theme Rule
rules.body: Every color is consumed through the CSS variables so both themes stay in step.

rules.name: The Figures First Rule
rules.body: Money amounts get the heaviest weight in their container and always show the ₱ symbol.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Floating Rule
rules.body: A surface gets blur or shadow only if it floats above other content.

dos: Do use the CSS variables for every color so light and dark both work.
Do keep touch targets at least 40px high and focus rings visible (WCAG 2.1 AA).
Do format all amounts with the currency pipe (PHP, ₱).
donts: Don't use emerald, amber or rose for decoration.
Don't add shadows or blur to resting cards.
Don't convey meaning by color alone; pair it with a sign, label or icon.
